Knowledge Topic

Electrical Parameters

Definitions and selection effects of capacity, voltage ratio, frequency, vector group, impedance, insulation level and tap range.

On this pageRatingsSystem compatibilityVoltage regulationRelated FAQs

Ratings

Rated capacity and voltage define the basic electrical duty but do not fully define the transformer design.

System compatibility

Frequency, phase, vector group, grounding and impedance affect system integration and parallel operation.

Voltage regulation

OCTC and OLTC arrangements provide different methods of adjusting transformer ratio.

Related questions

FAQ

What is transformer K-factor?

K-factor indicates the transformer's ability to carry specified nonlinear load currents without exceeding its thermal limits.

Read engineering answer →

FAQ

What is transformer impedance voltage and why does it matter?

Impedance voltage affects fault current, voltage regulation, load sharing and the ability of transformers to operate in parallel.

Read engineering answer →

FAQ

What is the difference between OLTC and OCTC?

An OLTC changes transformer taps while energized and carrying load, while an OCTC is operated only when the transformer is de-energized.

Read engineering answer →

FAQ

What is a transformer vector group?

The vector group identifies winding connections, neutral availability and the phase displacement between transformer windings.

Read engineering answer →
